title: The "King Carter" name and Irving Mills's Royal Orchestra plan
summary: Carter explains how the King Carter name came from Mills's planned royal orchestras and says he had nothing to do with those recordings.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: It was around that time, I think, that you had another association, didn't you, with Irving Mills -- and something connected with the title -- the royal title you got of King Carter. Who called you 'King Carter' in the first instance? Do you remember that?
Well, in the first instance, I'm not

sure, but I do know that at one period, Irving Mills was talking about the idea of having -- what was it -- the Royal Orchestra, Inc. --and he was ... I think the idea stemmed from having Duke Ellington.
Right.
And he was going to sign Earl Hines and he had an orchestra called Baron Lee.
Right.
I think that was Jimmy Ferguson, a comedian. And King Carter. Now that was where the King Carter came from.
Was it he who gave you that name, or was it ...
Well, some musicians already started calling me that, you know; I don't remember whether it was before or after.
And what became of that plan? I guess there were some recordings we know that there are recordings and discographies under the name King Carter.
Right.
Did you have anything to do with those?
No.
Nothing?
No.
The name ... you had given permission for the name to be used, or did it sort of refer to you?

Well, that's a very strange thing, because at this moment, I can't recall -- maybe they may have even felt ... when I say 'they' I mean the Mills organization, -- they may have felt that they owned the name as they owned Baron Lee. Duke Ellington was, of course, Duke Ellington's name, Earl Hines was his name -- so they wouldn't have owned that. But King Carter was not necessarily my name, nor was it a name that I went by as a nickname at that time.
And they recorded -- that the King Carter group recorded "Blues in My Heart".
Yes. Would that have been King Carter and the Blue Rhythm Orchestra?
That's right. That was another name ....
Mills Blue Rhythm Orchestra, yes.
